_meta.title: Current-law federal fiscal baseline, FY2025
_meta.note: This is the tool's 'you are here'. FY2025 is the latest complete fiscal year. Use OMB AP-8 line items for composition (they itemize and sum exactly); use CBO for totals and ratios.

receipts._note: OMB's seven-line taxonomy is the only published set that itemizes AND sums exactly. CBO's five-bucket presentation collapses excise + estate/gift + miscellaneous into one 'Other Receipts' line of $183B. The dossier's '~$379B other receipts' figure was an error: it double-counted customs duties as both its own line and part of 'other'. Resolved.

individual_income_tax.source: OMB, FY2027 Budget Analytical Perspectives, Ch. 8 Governmental Receipts, Table 08-1

corroborating.source: CBO, Monthly Budget Review: Fiscal Year 2025 final

payroll_social_insurance.note: Payroll tax is the largest federal tax for most households. See history-series.json > payroll for the rate/cap series.

corporate_income_tax.note: CBO's MBR shows corporate receipts FELL 14.7% from FY2024 ($530B) to FY2025 ($452B).

customs_duties.note: Up 153% year over year per CBO ('Customs Duties (including tariffs) | 80 | 77 | 195 | 153.0'). This is the tariff story and it is a genuinely new feature of the FY2025 baseline — worth an Act 1 annotation.

corroborating.source: CBO, The Accuracy of CBO's Budget Projections for Fiscal Year 2025
corroborating.note: reports FY2025 actual excise taxes of $106 billion

estate_and_gift_taxes.note: Fell 7% from FY2024 (~$31.7B) per CBO. Against roughly $3T/yr of wealth transfers. This is 0.56% of federal receipts — the framing number for the estate-tax era card.

miscellaneous_receipts.note: Federal Reserve remittances sit inside this line and are not separately published. Do NOT derive the Fed component from CBO's 'increased by $2 billion (or 75 percent)' — that is arithmetic on a rounded delta. See blocked.json.

total.note: CBO prints $5,235B; the $1.4B gap is a receipts-taxonomy difference between the two agencies, not an error in either. Components above sum to 5,236.4 exactly.

total_pct_gdp.source: CBO, The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036, Table 1-1
total_pct_gdp.note: SUPERSESSION: CBO's Nov 2025 final MBR says 17.3% and OMB's April 2026 AP-8 still prints 17.3%. Both used a pre-revision GDP. BEA's revised FY2025 GDP of $30,362B puts it at 17.2%. Ship 17.2% and footnote that earlier CBO releases show 17.3%, or a reader checking the MBR will think the tool is wrong.

total.source: CBO, Monthly Budget Review: Fiscal Year 2025 final
total.quote: Outlays in fiscal year 2025 were $7.0 trillion

total_pct_gdp.source: CBO, The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036, Table 1-1

discretionary_defense.source: CBO, Discretionary Spending in Fiscal Year 2025: An Infographic
discretionary_defense.note: OUTLAYS, not budget authority. 2.9% of GDP.

discretionary_nondefense.source: CBO, Discretionary Spending in Fiscal Year 2025: An Infographic

discretionary_total.source: CBO, Discretionary Spending in Fiscal Year 2025
discretionary_total.quote: Discretionary outlays by the federal government totaled $1.9 trillion in 2025. Outlays for nondefense programs accounted for more than half of that total.
discretionary_total.note: ANCHOR-FACT GATE: the tool's claim that tax expenditures exceed all discretionary spending must clear $1,873B, not the ~$1,800B the dossier's inputs implied. It still clears — JCT's FY2026 tax expenditure total is $2,300B — but by $427B, not $500B. State the comparison with both figures and both periods (FY2026 expenditures vs FY2025 outlays), since they are different years.

deficit.source: CBO, Monthly Budget Review: Fiscal Year 2025 final
deficit.quote: The federal budget deficit totaled $1.8 trillion—a decrease of $41 billion (or 2 percent) from the shortfall recorded in the previous year.

pct_gdp.source: CBO, The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036, Table 1-1
pct_gdp.note: Same GDP-revision supersession as receipts. The Nov 2025 MBR says 5.9%.

fy2025_nominal.source: CBO, The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036, Table 1-1
fy2025_nominal.note: Use this, not the dossier's back-solved ~$30.26T. Check: 5,235 / 30,362 = 17.24%, matching CBO's printed 17.2%.

cy2025_nominal.source: BEA NIPA via FRED series GDPA

latest_quarterly_nominal.source: BEA NIPA via FRED series GDP (advance estimate)
latest_quarterly_nominal.note: SAAR. Advance estimate; the second estimate is due later in August 2026 and will revise it. Label as 'advance estimate, July 30, 2026' anywhere it is shown.

cbo_2026_projected.source: CBO, The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036
cbo_2026_projected.note: Use this as the denominator for 'one point of GDP is worth $X' framing. See derived.point_of_gdp.

latest_real_growth.source: BEA, Gross Domestic Product, 2nd Quarter 2026 (Advance Estimate), BEA 26-35
latest_real_growth.quote: Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 1.5 percent in the second quarter of 2026
latest_real_growth.note: Q1 2026 was 2.1 percent. Current-dollar GDP rose at a 7.9 percent SAAR.

gdp_composition._note: All levels are BEA via FRED, same vintage (Q2 2026 advance, released 2026-07-30). Shares are arithmetic on the verified levels. Identity check: 22,078.176 + 5,719.908 - 869.026 + 5,546.153 = 32,475.211 vs printed GDP 32,475.210 (0.001 rounding). These are Q2 2026, NOT FY2025 — do not put them on the same axis as the budget figures without saying so.

government_g.quote: Government Consumption Expenditures and Gross Investment ... Q2 2026: 5,546.153

net_exports_nx.quote: Net Exports of Goods and Services ... Q2 2026: -869.026

federal_purchases.quote: Federal Consumption Expenditures and Gross Investment ... Q2 2026: 1,988.449
federal_purchases.note: TEACHING POINT, and a strong one: total federal OUTLAYS are 23.1% of GDP, but federal PURCHASES — goods and services the government actually buys, the 'G' in GDP — are 6.1%. The ~17-point gap is transfers, grants to states, and interest: money that moves without the federal government buying anything, so it shows up in GDP as C or I or state/local G. Note the two figures are different bases (FY2025 budget vs Q2 2026 NIPA) and different accounting concepts; do not subtract them on screen.

point_of_gdp.source: CBO, The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036
point_of_gdp.note: The dossier's $290B corresponds to a ~$29T GDP, a 2024-vintage figure. Express as 'about $320 billion' rather than $319B — the underlying GDP is a projection and false precision is unwarranted. ARITHMETIC IS OURS, the GDP level is CBO's; label it as a derivation in the methodology page.

vintage_warnings: Two live percent-of-GDP vintages exist for FY2025. Nov 2025 final MBR: receipts 17.3%, deficit 5.9%. Feb/Mar 2026 CBO: 17.2%, 5.8%. Dollar figures are identical across all releases; only the GDP denominator moved. Publish the 2026 vintage, footnote the 2025 one.
CBO's September 2025 MBR (published Oct 8, 2025) is STALE: outlays $7,035B, deficit $1,809B, individual income tax $2,665B, payroll $1,730B. Use only the Nov 10, 2025 final.
GDP composition is Q2 2026; the budget data is FY2025. Never present them as one time series.
